column2: Why does deficiency of a vitamin-derived cofactor impair several pathways at once?
column3: The cofactor serves multiple enzymes sharing the same chemical task, so deficiency affects them all rather than one isolated pathway.

column2: Why does thiamine deficiency particularly harm brain and heart and cause lactic acidosis?
column3: Thiamine pyrophosphate is needed by pyruvate dehydrogenase and other oxidative enzymes; these organs depend on continuous oxidative metabolism, and impaired pyruvate use causes lactic acidosis.

column3: NAD generally carries electrons from catabolic reactions toward energy production, whereas NADP provides reducing power for biosynthesis and antioxidant defence.
